description: A novel sieve eliminates >99% of candidate numbers from Collatz delay searches using modular arithmetic. By precomputing which residue classes mod 2^k must produce shorter trajectories, we skip directly to numbers whose binary structure forces long odd-step chains. This is the computational backbone of the delay record hunter.
mathematical_formalization: For sieve width w = 2^k, partition Z into residue classes r mod w. For each r, simulate k steps of the shortcut Collatz map T(n) = (3n+1)/2 if odd, n/2 if even. Discard r if the trajectory drops below r within k steps. Surviving fraction ~ (3/4)^k * correction. With k=32, survival rate < 0.008.
analogical_connections: Like the Sieve of Eratosthenes eliminates composites, this eliminates 'short-trajectory' residue classes
Analogous to branch prediction in CPU pipelines - predicting which numbers will 'branch' into long trajectories
Similar to how restriction enzymes in molecular biology cut DNA at specific recognition sites, the sieve cuts the search space at predictable modular sites
implementation_hypothesis: Precompute a lookup table of size 2^k mapping each residue class to (steps_taken, resulting_residue, odd_count, even_count). Only iterate numbers where odd_count/even_count > 0.60 (high completeness candidates).
experiment_seed: Compare wall-clock time to find all delay records below 10^12 with sieve widths k=16, 20, 24, 28, 32. Measure fraction of numbers surviving vs theoretical (3/4)^k.
